name: De L'Europe
positioning: Historic Amsterdam hotel, officially De L'Europe Amsterdam, open since 1896 on the Amstel River and owned by the HEINEKEN company
best_for: Travelers who want a historic hotel on the Amstel in central Amsterdam
Design and art lovers drawn to the partner-designed 't Huys suites

facts.text: The hotel first opened its doors as Hotel De L'Europe on 23 September 1896.
The hotel stands exactly where Het Rondeel, one of the main towers of Amsterdam's old city wall, once stood.
Alfred 'Freddy' Heineken bought the hotel after frequenting it, and today it is owned by the HEINEKEN company.
In 2020 the hotel had a complete redesign, with Dutch interior designers Nicemakers restyling the rooms, public areas, private event rooms, three restaurants and the bar.
The hotel's restaurants include Restaurant Flore, Brasserie Marie and Trattoria Graziella.
Freddy's Bar is named after Alfred 'Freddy' Heineken, who used to relax there.
Freddy's Bar hosts live jazz and works on a walk-in basis, with no reservation needed.
The spa has a heated indoor pool, saunas, relaxation areas and a fitness studio.
The spa offers Biologique Recherche facial treatments.
The hotel sits at the crossroads of the Amstel River and the Rokin canal.
The One-Bedroom Prestige Apartment has a fully equipped kitchen and is aimed at longer stays.
The hotel is wheelchair friendly and has four elevators, including access to the spa.

highlights.text: The suites in the 't Huys wing are each designed by a local partner, and each comes with experiences linked to that partner.
Overnight guests get complimentary access to the spa and wellness facilities throughout their stay.
Afternoon tea is served in a setting overlooking the Amstel River, and on the terrace on warmer days with good weather.
The Wunderkammer atelier in 't Huys displays floral works of art, interior objects and curiosities by floral artists Florian Seyd and Ueli Signer.
Purchases at the IN-HUYS concept store, which features products by local designers, can be added to the room bill.

considerations.text: The afternoon tea is served only on Saturday and Sunday afternoons and cannot offer lactose-free or gluten-free options.
There is no kids club or specific family program, but rooms from the premium deluxe category can interconnect.
WhataHotel notes the busy city-centre setting may bring some street noise for light sleepers.
